checks.detail: No scheduler job exists until explicit activation. The separate RAM consent, fresh capability and exact mailbox/organization/date selection are required. No cron or persisted credential is added.

The unchanged gateway authenticates the captured bearer through Auth and tc_verified_session. Grant claims are decoded only after verification; actor/SID/AAL and fresh company write/features are checked before effects. UI context and pending-start invalidation remain in place.

Canonical timestamps, fixed original dates, at most one hour and Madrid day end, native SID/AAL binding and request narrowing are enforced. Signed continuations bind the original grant period, account, identity, start and expiry. Repeated/no-progress continuations stop the coordinator.

Grant expiry is checked again after awaited permissions/AI availability. Stopping an account also aborts pending activation. The provider checks account/scope/visibility/connectivity again after status awaits; stopped flights cannot update a replacement job.

Automatic requests stop after one new original or the first incidence; candidate/byte/message bounds remain. Manual requests retain ten attachments. Existing private originals, content-hash deduplication, unique invoice reservation and conservative unknown-usage reservation are unchanged. No SQL, quota or provider-setting change is introduced.

Supplemental privacy describes the opt-in foreground scope and limits without replacing previous contractual consent. No new sensitive logging or WebStorage is introduced; fixed HTTPS destinations, no redirects, pinned public IMAP DNS/strict TLS and disabled transport logging remain.

Five minutes, ten batches and one active flight are coordinator controls. The documentation separately attributes one new original per automatic request and existing AI reservations/quotas to the backend; it does not describe min5/max10 as a remote rate limiter.

operating_limits: Coordinator interval, request ceiling, visibility and concurrency are per running app instance. They are not a global remote rate limiter across tabs, devices, direct callers or legacy manual requests; the server retains its existing authorization and AI quotas.

A grant is a transient request acknowledgement rather than a persisted contractual receipt. App visibility and explicit human interaction are enforced by the client workflow; the server independently verifies the bearer, scope, dates and supplied grant expiry.

Stopping removes subsequent app work and discards late UI results. A request or model call already accepted may complete; saved originals remain private. Uncertain provider usage retains its conservative reservation and is not automatically retried.

AI readiness indicates configuration/permission availability, not a reserved remaining budget. An original can be saved before AI budget denial; the resulting incidence stops automatic work and requires review.

Gmail/IMAP pagination or UIDVALIDITY changes can stop a traversal. Exhausting ten batches before catch-up completes requires explicit review/reactivation; no silent cursor reset or date expansion is promised.
This review does not constitute a new live mailbox, Google public-verification, managed recovery, physical-device or model/provider acceptance. No live calls were repeated.
